answers.answer: Shuffle Factory cards, deal number of players + 1 face-down on the board, return others unseen; place one random structure bonus tile face-up below Popularity Track; put tokens on each of the 11 marked territories. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: “number of players + 1”; “11 marked territories”; “lowest-numbered Player Mat starts”.

answers.answer: Character starts at home base; two workers start on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining it; four mechs are placed over Faction Mat abilities; six stars by faction emblem; six tech cubes in black-square green boxes; four structures in matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits on bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside Player Mat. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins and two objectives.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 3–4, including “Use the Faction Mat” and “Use the Player Mat”.

answers.answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action. Rusviet may repeat a section; others may not. If taking both actions, take top before bottom; top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before choosing any amount of exposed green-box benefits, which may be declined; exact costs/benefits follow your mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “must move”; “bottom first is not allowed”; “First pay the full cost”; “use top-row gains to pay the bottom-row cost”.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls that territory and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure’s abilities; you retain its abilities except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Pay costs with resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: “An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls it”; resources may be used from “any territories you currently control”.

answers.answer: No: normal Move selects up to two different units and moves each one adjacent territory, so one unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A worker carried by a mech may subsequently move itself, or may board a mech and be carried by its later move. All units (characters, mechs, workers) can carry any number of resources; only mechs also carry any number of your workers, never your character.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: “two different units”; carried worker “may subsequently move itself”; “Only mechs may also carry” workers.

answers.answer: The Speed-enabled mech stops and cannot move again that turn when it enters enemy-worker-only territory; those workers immediately retreat home, leaving resources, and you lose one popularity per worker down to zero. Zero popularity does not prevent retreat. Its transported workers cannot independently enter territory controlled by enemy workers (a worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory).
answers.evidence: Move: enemy workers “immediately retreat”; “insufficient popularity does not prevent the retreat”; worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.

answers.answer: After all units finish moving, resolve any combats before the bottom-row action; attacker chooses the order when there are multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: finish moving other units then resolve combats “before the bottom-row action”; “attacker chooses multiple-combat order”; worker entry/exit restriction.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card (before upgrades); if draw deck is empty, shuffle discards, and if both piles are empty draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity (before upgrades); traded resources go on a controlled territory with at least one worker. You cannot Trade for resources if all workers are at home.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade action descriptions.

answers.answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one terrain-matching token onto that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including workers; new workers alter future Produce costs only, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps 1–3: pay “in full before production”; workers taken “left to right”; “affects future Produce actions”.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes; Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes (amount depends on mat/upgrades). Upgrade moves a cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost; solid-black-bordered red boxes are ineligible. Deploy puts a chosen mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake; its uncovered ability then applies to your character and all mechs, not workers. Even after completing all such pieces, you may still pay for the bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade, Deploy, and opening paragraph on completing pieces.

answers.answer: Build on a controlled territory with your worker; only one structure total per territory, including opponents’; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A controlled Mill grants its bonus production territory; it cannot produce when uncontrolled. A Mine is your personal tunnel for your units even when its territory is enemy-controlled, subject to normal entry/combat restrictions.
answers.evidence: Build description; Mill exception in Produce; Mine personal tunnel in Move.

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section, put it permanently on any open one-time bonus space on your Faction Mat, and immediately get two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. Its ongoing bonus is set by the Player Mat circle uncovered by removing it: Upgrade +1 power, Deploy +1 coin, Build +1 popularity, Enlist +1 combat card. For you/left/right triggers resolve active player, then left, then right, stopping if a sixth star ends game; in two-player play the opponent triggers it once.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits sections.

answers.answer: Both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power 0 through the lesser of seven and current power, and may add up to one card per participating character/mech; People's Army adds one total card if a worker is present. If both have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, defender second. Reveal simultaneously, add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Both deduct chosen dial power from Power Track and discard played cards face-up; card values do not cost track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–4.

answers.answer: Winner controls territory/resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally at most two; Saxony unrestricted within six). All losing characters, mechs and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources; Nordic Seaworthy permits eligible retreat to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; winning defender loses none, with Polania Camaraderie exception. Loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 5–6.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve encounter if the character remains there; discard token and draw card. If contested entry is lost, character retreats and token stays. All resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory where character is. Pay printed encounter cost, but no additional normal action cost and no mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses apply.
answers.evidence: Encounters section: “after ... all combats”; token remains if lost; gains go to “encounter territory”; no normal action costs/bonuses.

answers.answer: Every player’s character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), looks at available cards, chooses one, and returns the rest; each player gets at most one permanent card and later visits cannot exchange it. A card is a fifth action section under normal top-then-bottom/no-repeat rules (Rusviet exception), but similar Factory actions give no mat coins, structure bonuses or recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories, or Speed character/mech up to three, subject to normal movement, Mine and stop rules.
answers.evidence: Factory section.

answers.answer: Reveal a completed objective only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, and meet all requirements at reveal; you may wait. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star; Saxony keeps the other card and may score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements section.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Goals are awarded once except combat stars/Saxony exception; stars are permanent even if power/popularity later drops, and other players’ stars do not block a goal. The sixth star ends play immediately, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end section.

answers.answer: For a sixth star from a bottom-row action, first collect the primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. If battle units remain intermingled in unresolved combat, undo that movement and return initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish active action, then check active player, left neighbor, right neighbor in that order, stopping after a sixth star so later stars/bonuses do not resolve.
answers.evidence: Sixth-star timing paragraphs.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity use the 7–12 tier: five stars score $20 ($4 each); four normal territories plus Factory count as 7, scoring $21 ($3 each); 13 resources make six complete pairs, scoring $12 ($2 each). These categories add $53 to held coins, plus the selected structure bonus. Structure bonus is earned even if enemies control your structure territories, but amount cannot be determined without knowing the selected tile and qualifying structures. Tiebreakers: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and “Structure bonus: Earn it even if enemies control” plus tiebreak list; selected tile/structure layout are unspecified.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory. Normally you cannot move back into any home base, build there, or deploy there; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea’s unlocked Wayfare. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases.

answers.answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, villages workers; lakes and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; resource definition and supply limit.

answers.answer: All units may pick up, carry and drop resources, including mid-movement; a mech may pick up/drop workers mid-movement. Mechs carry your workers but never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers; a tunnel jump costs one step, with extra step before or after, while stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move action carrying rules and Speed paragraph.

answers.answer: Yes, any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy-structure-only territory and printed tunnel rules.

answers.answer: Do not pay a partial Produce cost. If unable to afford any action, move the token to a different section and take neither action (a dead turn).
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Never pay only part of a cost”; dead turn description.

answers.answer: Armory grants +1 power on Trade; Monument grants +1 popularity on Bolster. These are built-structure bonuses for matching future top actions. You retain structure abilities even without control, so an enemy occupant cannot take them away; exception: Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory.
answers.evidence: Trade/Bolster and control sections; structure abilities retained without control.

answers.answer: Riverwalk gives character/mechs these destinations: Rusviet farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Nordic forests and mountains; Polania villages and mountains; Saxony forests and mountains. Nordic Swim instead lets workers alone cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes; it does not help character/mechs and gives no lake movement.
answers.evidence: Faction Riverwalk table and Nordic Swim description.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including your Mine) adjacent; Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent. These are shortcuts for character/mech Move actions.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine: opponent loses two power on track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery may be paid before combat: pay one power to reduce opponent’s power by two, also once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Saxony Disarm and Nordic Artillery descriptions.

answers.answer: Two mechs and three workers allow three combat cards total with People's Army (one per participating character/mech plus one additional card total when at least one worker is present). Workers alone never fight.
answers.evidence: Rusviet People's Army: “Two mechs and three workers allow three cards”; combat says workers alone never fight.

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to your own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. It cannot enter an active opponent’s home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare description.

answers.answer: Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion lets you spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of card value.
answers.evidence: Crimea Scout and Coercion descriptions.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake, but has no Nordic adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes require a mech to move off; carried workers/resources cannot be left behind on a lake when carrier leaves.
answers.evidence: Nordic Seaworthy, Polania Submerge, and lake carrier rules.

answers.answer: Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn. It does not protect against popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Polania Camaraderie description.

answers.answer: Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; the first gain may pay the second option’s cost. The summary does not state a special exemption from paying the printed cost of each chosen option; encounter costs must be paid, with benefits optionally taken in part or whole.
answers.evidence: Polania Meander table; Encounter options/cost paragraph.

answers.answer: No. A character entering an encounter territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move. Resolve the encounter only after the whole Move action and all combats, if character remains there.
answers.evidence: Move encounter stop rule; Encounters applies during Factory Move and resolves after all combats.

answers.answer: Combat-card count is public but contents secret; objective contents are secret. Coins are not hidden information, but a player need not reveal their total coin value.
answers.evidence: Setup information paragraph.

answers.answer: Only coins are tangible items exchangeable; agreements are informal and unenforceable. Tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances. A payment cannot cancel combat already initiated by moving units onto opposing units; combat happens after Move, though bribes may influence outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements section.

answers.answer: Popularity 0–6: $3 per star, $2 per territory count, $1 per complete resource pair; 7–12: $4, $3, $2; 13–18: $5, $4, $3. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Score each complete pair and ignore odd leftover resources.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and territory/resource income rules.

answers.answer: Only the selected tile scores and adjacency features count uniquely across all structures; rivers do not break adjacency. Tunnel tile counts unique printed tunnels, not Mines: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6=$9. Encounter tile counts unique printed encounter locations even if token removed: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9. Lake tile counts unique lakes: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table and adjacency rule.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels count structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. Structures in a row score only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break it: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Structures on farms/tundras count qualifying structures combined: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake, unless Polania Camaraderie applies under its conditions.
answers.evidence: Combat step 6.

answers.answer: No. A popularity star remains permanently placed, but current popularity (not the star) determines final scoring tier. Other players’ stars never block an achievement, so two factions can each star the same goal.
answers.evidence: Stars section: star permanent even if popularity drops; current popularity scores; “Other players’ stars never block a goal.”

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order clockwise: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Relative seating matters because ongoing recruit bonuses trigger for the active player and immediate left and right neighbors.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2–3 and Ongoing recruits.

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with applicable lake movement may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Move river/lake movement rules.

answers.answer: No, the card is not private: show it to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud. You need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: “Show the encounter card to all players”; show artwork and read capitalized text.

answers.answer: There is no limit on friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: “No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.”

answers.answer: The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure or recruit to gain. Interactive bonuses and end-game priority are resolved in order.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure timing paragraph.

answers.answer: No. You may take a section’s top action once and bottom action once in a turn; the token must move to a different section from last turn. Rusviet may repeat a section, including Factory card, across turns.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: top/bottom each “once”; different section; Rusviet repeat.

answers.answer: You may gain $1 instead of moving units with the normal unupgraded Move action.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: “Alternatively gain $1.”

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat; workers retreat to home base and do not return to the mat, so they cannot be reused to cover Produce cost boxes.
answers.evidence: Produce: “Workers never return to the Player Mat”; enemy-worker retreat destination is home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity, including both at zero.
answers.evidence: Combat: “You may attack with zero power/popularity.”

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; the ordinary two combat stars limit star placement, not further combats.
answers.evidence: Combat step 5: “You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit.”

answers.answer: For a faction without Meander, you must choose one affordable option and cannot decline all options; unaffordable coin/popularity options cannot be selected. You may take as little of the chosen option’s benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters: must choose “one affordable option”; unaffordable options barred; benefit may be partial.

answers.answer: No. Both combatants choose secretly and simultaneously, not in turn order; reveal dials and card choices simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3.

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: “Announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.”

answers.answer: No. Star goals are awarded as soon as achieved; the sixth star immediately ends play, so you cannot delay or decline it. A completed objective is different: you may wait to reveal it, but must meet all requirements at the moment you eventually reveal it on your turn.
answers.evidence: Stars: “Place a star as soon as you achieve”; Objectives: “You may wait” to reveal.

answers.answer: Normally none of a character, mech or worker can cross rivers or enter lakes; faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.
answers.evidence: Move: units “cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes.”

answers.answer: No. The recruit is permanently placed on the one-time bonus space and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: “It cannot later move.”

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering the territory does not trigger or remove its token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: “Only a character triggers an encounter.”

answers.answer: A controlled Mill adds one bonus production territory to your normal allowance: normally up to three total, or up to four if upgraded allowance is three. Mill itself counts as one producing worker and produces terrain output even without an actual worker there; actual workers at the Mill each produce normally too, so Mill output is added rather than substituted. It only works while controlled.
answers.evidence: Produce Mill paragraph.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish control, so after your last unit leaves a territory without your structure you do not control it.
answers.evidence: Control definition: unit there or structure with no enemy unit.

answers.answer: Build costs wood; Enlist costs food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: “Upgrade — oil”; “Deploy — metal”; “Build — wood”; “Enlist — food”.
